notes:
High-level: NimbusCare runs 24/7 telehealth contact centers (heavy PHI). Looking to replace their current mix: OpenAI-hosted API for chat and an internal vendor-x runtime for on-prem inference. Main ask: agent-assist + ticket summarization with deterministic behavior under spikes and strict PHI controls.

Recent timeline / activity (bullets):
- 2026-02-11: Intro call (Arielle + Diego) with CTO Maya Lin and Head of Support Ravi Patel — Fireflies ff-2026-02-11-7f3c.
- 2026-02-18: Security questionnaire submitted; security team requested SOC2 and ISO evidence + DPA template. (drive://NimbusCare/Security-FAQ-answers-v2.md)
- 2026-02-25: Tech deep-dive with SE (Diego) — went through model routing, KV caching, tool-calling for EHR integration.
- 2026-03-02: Perf baseline call; shared current vendor metrics (p50 latency 140ms, >2s tail during spikes). Fireflies ff-2026-03-02-1b9a.
- 2026-03-04: POC scope approved internally; legal started DPA addendum review.

POC scope (agreed):
- 2-week sandbox in dedicated pool + VPC peering to their staging network.
- Workload: agent-assist (real-time suggestions), ticket summarization (end-of-conversation summaries), selective tool-calling into CRM/EHR (update ticket status, fetch patient consent flags).
- Targets: median latency <= 150ms for agent-assist tokens, 95th percentile < 400ms under 200 concurrent agents.
- Throughput/spike requirement: absorb up to 4x traffic during promo windows with graceful degradation to lightweight quantized model and cached responses.
- Quality: extractive + abstractive summaries with preserve PHI redaction rules; human-in-the-loop monitor for first 2k tickets.

Migration notes / competitive positioning:
- Current pain: vendor-x runtime has unpredictable tail latency during spikes; OpenAI hosted solves latency but fails on residency/HIPAA controls.
- NimbusCare wants unified API/ops across hosted/dedicated/private — strong reason to consider Redwood.
- Key asks vs competitors: predictable SLOs for spikes, private VPC option, audit logs for every call, KMS-encrypted model keys, and A/B rollback for model regressions.

Customer quotes / paraphrases:
- "We need a fallback path that doesn't create crazy hallucinations when we go to quantized models." — Ravi Patel, Head of Support.
- "If we can't get legal to sign a HIPAA addendum quickly, we can't start the POC." — Maya Lin, CTO.

Technical risks identified:
- Summarization regressions after aggressive quantization; want baseline eval suite (100 tickets) to detect regressions.
- Tool-calling safety: need confirm/consent flow & idempotency checks.
- Network egress and VPC peering latency during peaky loads.

Docs / artifacts referenced:
- Redwood POC deck (shared) -> drive://NimbusCare/Redwood-POC-Deck-2026.pdf
- Security questionnaire reply (internal) -> drive://NimbusCare/Security-FAQ-answers-v2.md
- Jira tickets to track escalations: INF-4123 (perf anomaly), SEC-9981 (DPA follow-up).

Next steps (practical):
- Redwood SE to run focused perf test in dedicated pool (3/10–3/12) with simulated 200 concurrent agents and 4x burst.
- Delivery: provide quantization profile recommendations and expected token-cost delta vs current stack.
- Legal: send HIPAA addendum + SOC2 evidence by 2026-03-10.
- Sales: proposed contract + ARR range sent; finance waiting on final numbers.

Short-term blockers (restate): DPA/HIPAA signature, verify no major summarization regressions after quantization, confirm burst SLA/auto-fallback behavior.

CRM-style action items (choppy):

- SE (Diego) to deliver perf run logs and quantization plan by 3/12.
- CSM (Lena) to prepare onboarding checklist for Dedicated pool once contract signed.

Internal notes: high potential mid-market AE motion -> likely expand to enterprise if POC succeeds. Upsell: Redwood Optimize + longer term Private deployment for PHI retention controls.
